title: Open model admission control and runtime sanity test spec
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Background: We routinely ingest community/open model weights into the Redwood model catalog. Current intake checks are inconsistent across teams, and runtime compatibility notes are scattered. This ticket clarifies the minimal acceptance criteria for admitting a new open model variant into the hosted catalog, defines a small set of automated runtime sanity tests (to run during intake and at each variant pin), and documents guidance for version pinning and fallback behavior. Goal: reduce catalog regressions, shorten time-to-onboard, and make rollback decisions deterministic.
scope: In scope: (1) A concise admission checklist that product, runtime, and infra teams can use; (2) A 10-minute automated runtime sanity suite covering model load, tokenization parity, short-generation correctness, KV cache warmstart, and memory footprint; (3) Pinning guidance for open variants (when to pin major vs patch, suggested TTL for automatic re-profiling); (4) Required metadata fields added to catalog entries (quantization, compatible runtime builds, recommended batch sizes).
out_of_scope: Full-scale performance profiling, long-run regression detection infrastructure, and legal review of community licenses (handled by Legal).
acceptance_criteria: A public-facing admission checklist doc exists (Confluence link) and is approved by Runtime and Security leads.
Automated runtime sanity test can be executed in CI against a candidate variant; pass/fail result and a short JSON summary are produced.
Catalog ingestion UI/API surface requires the new metadata fields and enforces presence of compatibility tags for hosted use.
Pinning guidance is added to onboarding playbook; examples for three common cases (minor tuning, quantized variant, experimental weights) are provided.
At least one pilot open-model intake uses the checklist and sanity tests end-to-end with documented outcomes.
decisions: Use a lightweight sanity suite (5–7 checks) not full benchmarking to keep intake fast.
Require explicit 'runtime_compat' tag with minimum runtime version and fallback variant key.
Default: pin new community variants to a minor-version-based policy (e.g., pin major+minor) until 2 successful production rollouts.
Security review required for any model that requests private/customer data access or custom KMS usage.
risks: Too-strict admission rules could slow community adoption; mitigated by a fast 'experimental' lane with extra telemetry.
Sanity tests may miss subtle quality regressions; mitigation: link to eval-runbook and require manual review for higher-risk variants.
Incomplete metadata by contributors leading to runtime mismatches; mitigation: catalog API enforces required fields and rejects incomplete intake.
open_questions: What exact thresholds for memory/latency should fail intake vs warn? (Runtime to propose defaults by 2026-03-18)
Should we allow automatic re-profiling of pinned variants after N days or only via manual trigger?
How to surface fallback choices in the console UI without exposing internal variant IDs?
implementation_notes: Runtime team to provide a minimal CI artifact that runs sanity checks against a model tarball and returns a standardized result.
Catalog UI changes: make 'runtime_compat' required and add an 'experimental' checkbox that routes variants to a lower-SLA pool.
PM to coordinate a pilot with Solutions Eng (customer: mid-market search SaaS) to validate pin guidance in production traffic.
Create a short post-mortem template to capture catalog admission failures for the first three months.
